nodes.label: Connectivity, retention, common witness and redundancy limits
nodes.statement: For every nonnegative n-by-n W with n>=2, the positive-edge graph is strongly connected iff for every nontrivial bipartition pi and every vertex i there exists an integer k with 1<=k<=2(n-1) and (W^k-W_pi^k)_[i,i]>0, where W_pi deletes all crossing edges. Parity broadcast on five bits retains one bit; invertible four-bit shift-XOR retains four. Identity and parity modes do not jointly witness full capacity and complete dependencies. nodes.label: Successor sets and nonadditive inheritance
nodes.statement: Individual-only categorical labels cannot encode arbitrary successor sets. For a nonnegative membership relation across unique-continuation and fission scenarios, assume full unique continuation gives q(A,B)=1, adding an equally full co-successor preserves that value, and equally full copies are symmetric. Then two full successors have total membership at least 2, incompatible with unit-sum normalization. Equal singleton inclusion marginals need not identify mu; equal singleton inheritance need not identify Gamma. Duplication violates conserved-mass and universal supermodularity; secret sharing violates universal submodularity.
nodes.domain: Existence counterexamples under FUNCTIONAL_CONTRACT. The normalization clause compares singleton/full-continuation and two-full-successor scenarios under the same calibrated membership rule; includes nonnegativity, full-unique value 1, co-successor preservation and symmetry. It is not a no-go for categorical probabilities over mutually exclusive outcomes.

nodes.label: Constant Bet Preserves the Unweighted Average Target
nodes.statement: For bounded adapted X_ij with conditional means mu_ij, a predictable empirical-Bernstein exponent with one frozen constant positive bet lambda_j over i has linear term N lambda_j (bar X_j - N^-1 sum_i mu_ij); varying bets instead generally target a weighted average when the conditional means differ.
nodes.domain: Finite N, one component j, X_ij in [0,1], predictable residual predictors in [0,1], constant lambda_j in (0,1), and the average conditional mean; no independence is required for this algebraic/martingale target identity.
nodes.scope: Finite N, one component j, X_ij in [0,1], predictable residual predictors in [0,1], constant lambda_j in (0,1), and the average conditional mean; no independence is required for this algebraic/martingale target identity.
nodes.source_lineage: Waudby-Smith and Ramdas predictable plug-in inequality plus an explicit constant-bet specialization to unequal conditional means.
nodes.proof: Replace the common conditional mean in each centered one-step factor by mu_ij. The one-step proof is unchanged. Constancy of lambda_j factors it from the sum, leaving the unweighted average conditional mean.
nodes.counterexamples_and_limits: With varying lambda_ij and unequal mu_ij the exponent controls a lambda-weighted target. Under dependence the average conditional mean can be random and is not silently a fixed superpopulation mean.

nodes.label: Frozen Constant-Bet Bounded-Martingale Coverage
nodes.statement: For m frozen bounded components, constant pilot-frozen bets lambda_j in (0,1), predictable predictors c_ij in [0,1], and L=log(2m/alpha), the W-scale intervals centered at bar W_j with half-width 2[L+g(lambda_j) sum_i(X_ij-c_ij)^2]/(N lambda_j) simultaneously cover all average conditional means with probability at least 1-alpha; for independent participant vectors these are exactly the R163 finite-design means.

nodes.source_lineage: Fan/Howard bounded exponential inequality, Waudby-Smith-Ramdas predictable plug-in construction, two-tail and m-component union bounds, and the R162 independent-pilot tower contract.
nodes.proof: Multiply the centered one-step exponential factors to obtain a nonnegative supermartingale, apply fixed-time Markov bounds to X and 1-X, union-bound two tails and m components, scale from X to W, and condition on every independent-pilot-selected plan.
nodes.counterexamples_and_limits: Not uniformly narrower than Hoeffding; bad predictors or large residuals can widen it. Variable bets generally change the target. Participant dependence, same-data family selection or invalid range assumptions break the R163 finite-design specialization.

nodes.label: Rare-Spike Additive Protection Is Necessary
nodes.statement: For the R163 rare-spike law, any coordinatewise interval that excludes mean zero whenever a component has no spikes has m-component simultaneous coverage at most (1-.95^N)^m; at N=36,m=8 this is 0.2531673184308581, and controlling this event alone at familywise alpha=.05 requires N at least 99.
nodes.domain: The explicit independent m-component rare-spike product law and coordinatewise procedures having the stated all-no-spike exclusion property.
nodes.scope: The explicit independent m-component rare-spike product law and coordinatewise procedures having the stated all-no-spike exclusion property.
nodes.source_lineage: Exact probability calculation extending the R163 rare-spike witness; no general minimax optimality claim.
nodes.proof: A no-spike component occurs with probability .95^N and forces failure by hypothesis. Independent components give probability (1-.95^N)^m of avoiding all such failures; solving 1-(1-.95^N)^m<=.05 yields N>=99.
nodes.counterexamples_and_limits: This is necessary only for procedures with the stated coordinatewise failure property and is not a sufficient sample-size theorem. Other spike counts can still cause failure.

nodes.label: Instrumented Anchor–Mediator–Backup–Consumer Architecture
nodes.statement: A prospective non-invasive participant-device loop realizes a report-independent physical anchor r, a logged live controller mediator k, declared backup routes z, and actual consumers u, with independent reversible interventions on r, k and route gates. The operational k is not asserted to be a hidden neural or complete body representation.
nodes.domain: One instrumented participant-device episode with calibrated safe perturbations; no apparatus or participant was tested in R167.
nodes.scope: One instrumented participant-device episode with calibrated safe perturbations; no apparatus or participant was tested in R167.
nodes.source_lineage: Concrete realization proposal for R166 W2-W5 using established intervention and route-audit ideas; no mechanism novelty claim.
nodes.proof: Constructive specification of physically inspectable states, reads, interventions and route gates.
nodes.counterexamples_and_limits: Sensory or motor perturbation alone is not do(k); hidden routes, off-target effects, invalid fidelity or safety failure block the application.

formal_contract_R167.object_domain: one actual instrumented loop with sorted anchor, mediator, backups and consumers
formal_contract_R167.quantifiers: there exists one declared candidate architecture; every named state and route must be physically realized and audited
formal_contract_R167.bearer_time_signature: controller state and participant-device process are distinct but nested actual occurrences within P/I
formal_contract_R167.purpose: Give W2-W5 a manipulable same-episode realization without report-defined ownership

nodes.label: Contextual Relevance Under Declared Redundancy
nodes.statement: For a declared finite deterministic Boolean consumer u=f(k,z), k contributes relative to the declared intervention closure iff there exists a backup context z with f(1,z) unequal to f(0,z); k is contextually indispensable iff the inequality holds in every declared context. Contribution and indispensability are distinct.
nodes.domain: All deterministic Boolean functions with one candidate input k and finitely many declared binary backup inputs; executable enumeration covers zero through three backups.
nodes.scope: All deterministic Boolean functions with one candidate input k and finitely many declared binary backup inputs; executable enumeration covers zero through three backups.
nodes.source_lineage: Elementary extensional dependence criterion specialized to R166 W5; Boolean function theory is not claimed as new.
nodes.proof: If all controlled contrasts vanish, f is extensionally independent of k; one nonzero contrast is a witness. The checker enumerates 65,812 functions for m=0..3.
nodes.counterexamples_and_limits: The theorem is relative to declared variables, deterministic Boolean outputs and intervention semantics; it does not establish closure of the real organization.

formal_contract_R167.object_domain: finite declared Boolean consumer and backup context set
formal_contract_R167.quantifiers: for every f and every declared context; relevance is existential and indispensability universal over z
formal_contract_R167.bearer_time_signature: one pre-compensation time slice; abstract f requires separate realization in an actual token
formal_contract_R167.purpose: Prevent redundant masking from being mistaken for no installed use

nodes.label: One Active Backup Masks a Real Primary Contribution
nodes.statement: In u=k OR z, changing k while z=1 leaves u unchanged, although changing k while z=0 changes u. Therefore one null mediator cut in an uncontrolled redundant context does not refute installed use of k.
nodes.domain: The declared deterministic binary OR consumer under controlled interventions on k and z.
nodes.scope: The declared deterministic binary OR consumer under controlled interventions on k and z.
nodes.source_lineage: Elementary redundancy countermodel specialized to the R166 mediation witness.
nodes.counterexamples_and_limits: A validated contextual matrix can resolve this declared model; omitted backups remain possible.

formal_contract_R167.object_domain: one Boolean primary and one Boolean backup route
formal_contract_R167.quantifiers: there exists a masking context z=1 and a revealing context z=0
formal_contract_R167.bearer_time_signature: same modeled consumer and pre-compensation time slice

nodes.label: Late Recovery Does Not Refute Earlier Primary Use
nodes.statement: For u_t=k_t OR z_t with z_(t+1)=z_t OR cut_t, cutting an initially active k makes the immediate pre-adaptation output differ from baseline but the later compensated output equal baseline. A late endpoint alone therefore does not refute prior installed use.
nodes.domain: The declared two-step deterministic binary compensation model.
nodes.scope: The declared two-step deterministic binary compensation model.
nodes.source_lineage: Elementary finite-state countermodel specialized to timing in R166 W4-W5.
nodes.proof: Baseline u0=1; immediate post-cut u0'=0; after z updates to one, u1'=1.
nodes.counterexamples_and_limits: The model is not asserted as universal physiology; it refutes only the late-null-to-no-prior-use inference.

formal_contract_R167.quantifiers: there exists the stated initial state and cut sequence
formal_contract_R167.bearer_time_signature: same bearer lineage but distinct pre-adaptation and post-compensation subintervals
formal_contract_R167.purpose: Require temporal indexing and prevent compensation false negatives

nodes.label: Invalid, Supported, Closure-Refuted, or Unresolved
nodes.statement: For one named candidate: identity, admissibility or fidelity failure yields INVALID_PROTOCOL; a valid pre-compensation contextual contrast yields PRIMARY_USE_SUPPORTED_RELATIVE_TO_CLOSURE; all valid null contrasts yield CANDIDATE_REFUTED_RELATIVE_TO_CLOSURE only with declared route closure and adequate sensitivity; every other case is UNRESOLVED. Compensation is recorded as an additional temporal flag.
nodes.domain: One predeclared operational mediator candidate, declared finite backup closure and predeclared null/sensitivity bounds.
nodes.scope: One predeclared operational mediator candidate, declared finite backup closure and predeclared null/sensitivity bounds.
nodes.source_lineage: R161 bounded three-way decision refined for same-token mediation, redundancy and compensation.
nodes.proof: Priority logic is exhaustively checked over 128 Boolean assignments; empirical clauses remain uninstantiated.
nodes.counterexamples_and_limits: Any omitted route can defeat closure; null without closure/sensitivity is unresolved and never no experience.

formal_contract_R167.object_domain: one candidate and its declared intervention closure
formal_contract_R167.quantifiers: all validity premises precede any support/refutation; refutation universally covers declared contexts only
formal_contract_R167.bearer_time_signature: same token lineage with pre-compensation contrasts separated from adapted endpoints
formal_contract_R167.purpose: Preserve falsifiability without overclaiming completeness or no experience

nodes.label: Operational Discharge of W2–W5, Neural and Semantic Claims Open
nodes.statement: If one common actual episode satisfies the grounded selector, typed Anchor–Bind–Use schema, every R166 W1-W6 clause, the R167 token-lineage and operational architecture contracts, and closure-relative support, then W2-W5 are operationally discharged for the declared participant-device relation. This does not identify a hidden neural or complete body representation, prove route completeness, derive C1, validate B_min, or make the relation a basal-experience gate.
nodes.domain: One common actual P/I/K/D/rho episode and one declared operational relation satisfying all premises simultaneously.
nodes.scope: One common actual P/I/K/D/rho episode and one declared operational relation satisfying all premises simultaneously.
nodes.source_lineage: Conditional application of R157, R159 and R166 to the new operational architecture and bounded triage.
nodes.proof: Bind every premise to the same actual lineage and indexed subintervals; the operational state/read audit supplies W2-W3, valid local interventions W4, and contextual route discrimination W5, while W1 and W6 remain unchanged.
nodes.counterexamples_and_limits: Failure of any all-of premise blocks the conclusion; C1 transport remains R166/R159 conditional and familiar mineness still requires independent B_min.

formal_contract_R167.object_domain: one actual declared operational body-frame relation
formal_contract_R167.quantifiers: every all-of premise holds simultaneously on the one application; no universal neural or experiential necessity claim
formal_contract_R167.bearer_time_signature: same P/I lineage, explicit subintervals, fixed K/D/rho except named interventions; C1 applies tokenwise only where admitted
formal_contract_R167.purpose: Turn the R166 witness sketch into a concrete but strictly bounded application route

nodes.label: Contextual Interventional Effect in a Declared Consumer Geometry
nodes.statement: For declared safe mediator interventions K0, actual backup context z and interventional consumer laws Q_{k,z}, define e(z)=sup_{k,k' in K0} d_F(Q_{k,z},Q_{k',z}), where the discriminator class F is fixed before results. Contextual use is existence of z with e(z)>0 relative to K0, Z and F; indispensability is a distinct universal condition.
nodes.domain: One pre-compensation subinterval of one R167 episode, one declared consumer, one declared intervention set and one fixed integral-probability metric.
nodes.scope: One pre-compensation subinterval of one R167 episode, one declared consumer, one declared intervention set and one fixed integral-probability metric.
nodes.source_lineage: R167 contextual effect generalized with standard integral-probability-metric notation; no new IPM theorem claimed.
nodes.proof: Definition; Boolean deterministic output difference is recovered as a special case under a separating discriminator class.
nodes.counterexamples_and_limits: A weak F can miss distributional changes; changing F after results changes the claim; abstract laws require separate physical realization.

formal_contract_R168.object_domain: one actual consumer route and declared stochastic intervention family
formal_contract_R168.quantifiers: supremum over declared k,k'; existential over z for contribution and universal only for indispensability
formal_contract_R168.bearer_time_signature: same actual lineage and pre-compensation interval; random laws remain distinct from samples and fitted latents
formal_contract_R168.purpose: Extend R167 use without conflating output samples, distributions or experience

nodes.label: Pointwise Sharp Undetected-Effect Envelope
nodes.statement: For 0<=e<=M, L-Lipschitz e on declared (Z,d), tested actual contexts s_i and valid upper bounds e(s_i)<=U_i, every compatible e satisfies e(z)<=E(z)=min{M,inf_i[U_i+L d(z,s_i)]}; E itself is compatible, so no uniformly smaller pointwise upper bound follows from those premises alone.
nodes.domain: Any declared metric context space with nonempty tested set and finite nonnegative M,L,U_i; executable checks cover finite line metrics.
nodes.scope: Any declared metric context space with nonempty tested set and finite nonnegative M,L,U_i; executable checks cover finite line metrics.
nodes.source_lineage: Standard Lipschitz cone/extension reasoning specialized to closure-relative mediator effects; no historical mathematical novelty claim.
nodes.proof: Lipschitzness gives every cone bound; infimum and cap give E. The infimum of same-constant cones and constant cap are L-Lipschitz, and E(s_i)<=U_i, making E admissible and pointwise sharp.
nodes.counterexamples_and_limits: The physical metric, L and tested upper bounds are premises, not consequences; without them the numerical envelope has no physical authority.

formal_contract_R168.object_domain: bounded Lipschitz effect functions on a declared metric context space
formal_contract_R168.quantifiers: for every compatible e and every z; sharpness is pointwise over all compatible e
formal_contract_R168.bearer_time_signature: mathematical context geometry must be linked separately to actual episode contexts
formal_contract_R168.purpose: Quantify the strongest amplitude claim licensed by finite context tests and regularity

nodes.label: Observed Context Label Does Not Bound a Hidden Fiber
nodes.statement: If q(a)=q(b) and only actual context a is tested with e(a)=0, the compatible models e0(a)=e0(b)=0 and e1(a)=0,e1(b)=M agree on the observed label and tested law but differ maximally at b. Partial observation alone therefore yields no nontrivial hidden-fiber amplitude bound.
nodes.domain: A two-point hidden context space, one coarse observed label, one tested representative and effect range [0,M].
nodes.scope: A two-point hidden context space, one coarse observed label, one tested representative and effect range [0,M].
nodes.source_lineage: Elementary partial-identification counterexample specialized to R167 hidden redundancy.
nodes.proof: Direct construction; observed/tested objects are equal while hidden maxima are zero and M.
nodes.counterexamples_and_limits: A physically certified within-fiber regularity/lift premise can add a bound; the counterexample denies inference without it.

formal_contract_R168.object_domain: one coarse observation fiber with two actual hidden contexts
formal_contract_R168.quantifiers: there exist two compatible models with maximal hidden-effect separation
formal_contract_R168.bearer_time_signature: same observed label is not identity of actual physical context
formal_contract_R168.purpose: Block observed-label equality from masquerading as route closure

nodes.label: Section, Fiber Deviation, and Observed Coverage Contract
nodes.statement: For q:Z->X, require a declared section r, a within-fiber deviation d_Z(z,r(q(z)))<=delta, section regularity d_Z(r(x),r(x'))<=C d_X(x,x'), and tested observed fill distance h_X. These are independent physical/measurement premises, not consequences of sharing an observed label.
nodes.domain: One declared partial observation map and one actual context space with a chosen physical metric.
nodes.scope: One declared partial observation map and one actual context space with a chosen physical metric.
nodes.source_lineage: Explicit sufficient contract introduced to discharge the hidden-fiber obstruction; uses standard metric section reasoning.
nodes.proof: Contract definition; its consequence is registered separately.
nodes.counterexamples_and_limits: No section, delta or C is supplied by interface labels alone; a poor section can make the bound vacuous.

formal_contract_R168.object_domain: actual hidden contexts, observed contexts and a declared section
formal_contract_R168.quantifiers: every admissible z satisfies the fiber bound and every x,x' satisfy section regularity
formal_contract_R168.bearer_time_signature: r(x) denotes an actual tested-context representative, not an abstract label only
formal_contract_R168.purpose: State exactly what turns a partial interface into bounded actual-context coverage

nodes.label: Hidden-Context Fill Radius and Effect Bound
nodes.statement: Under the R168 partial-view lift contract, actual-context fill radius is at most delta+C h_X; combined with common tested effect upper eta and L-Lipschitz effect, sup_z e(z)<=min{M,eta+L(delta+C h_X)}.
nodes.domain: One common actual/observed metric application satisfying the section, fiber, coverage, effect-regularity and tested-bound premises simultaneously.
nodes.scope: One common actual/observed metric application satisfying the section, fiber, coverage, effect-regularity and tested-bound premises simultaneously.
nodes.source_lineage: Triangle inequality plus R168 sharp metric envelope.
nodes.proof: For any z choose nearest tested observed x_i; triangle inequality gives d_Z(z,r(x_i))<=delta+C h_X, then apply the common-upper fill-distance envelope.
nodes.counterexamples_and_limits: Invalid if the section is not physically realized, the fiber bound fails, or effect regularity does not hold; can be vacuous at M.

formal_contract_R168.quantifiers: for every admissible hidden context z under all simultaneous premises
formal_contract_R168.bearer_time_signature: same actual context geometry, section representatives and pre-compensation effect function
formal_contract_R168.purpose: Expose the hidden-fiber penalty instead of silently setting it to zero

nodes.label: No Detection Bounds Affected Context Mass Under Sampling
nodes.statement: If n contexts are sampled independently from declared mu and every sampled context with e(z)>tau is detected with probability at least s_min, no-detection probability is at most (1-s_min p)^n for p=mu{e>tau}; a no-hit 1-alpha upper bound is p<=min{1,(1-alpha^(1/n))/s_min}.
nodes.domain: Independent context draws, fixed affected set, fixed positive sensitivity lower bound and no adaptive post-result target changes.
nodes.scope: Independent context draws, fixed affected set, fixed positive sensitivity lower bound and no adaptive post-result target changes.
nodes.source_lineage: Elementary binomial no-hit calculation specialized to contextual mediator detection; no statistical novelty claim.
nodes.proof: Each draw detects with probability at least s_min p; independence multiplies no-detection probabilities, then invert the inequality.
nodes.counterexamples_and_limits: Bounds mu-mass only, not maximum amplitude or existence; invalid for dependent/adaptive draws, unknown mu, or unsupported sensitivity.

formal_contract_R168.object_domain: one declared context measure and affected-context event
formal_contract_R168.quantifiers: n independent draws; every affected draw has detection probability at least s_min
formal_contract_R168.bearer_time_signature: sampling distribution across contexts is not the complete organization of any one context
formal_contract_R168.purpose: Separate prevalence evidence from worst-case effect amplitude

nodes.label: Affected Mass and Maximum Effect Do Not Determine Each Other
nodes.statement: A no-hit mass bound does not bound sup_z e(z): arbitrarily large allowed effect can occupy an arbitrarily small or mu-null context. Conversely, large affected mass can have effect only infinitesimally above tau. Amplitude and prevalence are distinct evidence objects.
nodes.domain: Declared bounded effects and context measures; includes discrete and continuous examples.
nodes.scope: Declared bounded effects and context measures; includes discrete and continuous examples.
nodes.source_lineage: Elementary measure/amplitude separation specialized to hidden mediator effects.
nodes.proof: Put effect M on a set of arbitrarily small measure for high-amplitude/low-mass; put tau+epsilon on the full space for high-mass/low-excess.
nodes.counterexamples_and_limits: Metric regularity plus coverage can connect neighboring contexts, but only as an additional premise.

formal_contract_R168.object_domain: bounded effect functions and declared context measures
formal_contract_R168.quantifiers: there exist counterexample families in both directions
formal_contract_R168.bearer_time_signature: population over contexts remains distinct from an actual effect at a named context
formal_contract_R168.purpose: Prevent random coverage evidence from masquerading as closure or no effect

nodes.label: Invalid, Supported, Envelope-Refuted, Mass-Bounded, or Unresolved
nodes.statement: After all R167 validity gates: a tested lower bound above tau supports contextual use; a valid sharp envelope maximum at most tau refutes effects above tau relative to the declared envelope; a valid random-context no-hit result without amplitude closure bounds affected mass only; every remaining case is unresolved.
nodes.domain: One named operational mediator candidate, one fixed effect geometry, actual/partial context coverage and predeclared threshold tau.
nodes.scope: One named operational mediator candidate, one fixed effect geometry, actual/partial context coverage and predeclared threshold tau.
nodes.source_lineage: R167 closure-relative triage refined by sharp amplitude and affected-mass objects.
nodes.proof: Priority logic is exhaustively checked; mathematical bounds are supplied by the preceding nodes while empirical premises remain open.

formal_contract_R168.quantifiers: all validity premises precede status; local support is existential, envelope refutation universal over declared Z, mass bound relative to mu
formal_contract_R168.bearer_time_signature: same episode lineage and pre-compensation interval; samples, laws, contexts and experience remain distinct
formal_contract_R168.purpose: Make continuous/stochastic non-detection falsifiable without overclaiming

nodes.statement: If the complete R166 witness, R167 token-lineage/operational architecture, and every R168 effect, coverage, regularity and triage premise hold on one common actual episode, the stochastic/continuous evidence refines W4-W5 for that declared relation. It does not replace physical realization, identify neural completeness, derive C1, validate B_min, or create a basal-experience gate.
nodes.domain: One common actual P/I/K/D/rho episode and one fixed stochastic effect/coverage certificate satisfying all premises simultaneously.
nodes.scope: One common actual P/I/K/D/rho episode and one fixed stochastic effect/coverage certificate satisfying all premises simultaneously.

nodes.counterexamples_and_limits: Any unsupported metric, L, lift, sensitivity, route, identity or upper/lower bound blocks the refinement; abstract kernels do not install themselves.

formal_contract_R168.object_domain: one actual declared operational relation with stochastic consumer evidence
formal_contract_R168.quantifiers: every all-of premise holds on the same application; no universal necessity or familiar-mineness conclusion
formal_contract_R168.bearer_time_signature: same P/I lineage and indexed subinterval; actual routes, laws, samples, partial views, Phi/h and reports remain typed separately
formal_contract_R168.purpose: Extend operational installation evidence without weakening physical or semantic boundaries

nodes.statement: A declared route graph has actual admissible context states as typed nodes and only reversible, safe, fidelity-checked same-lineage context interventions as edges; task-label, fitted-latent or report adjacency is not an edge, and disconnected or omitted actual contexts receive no finite path bound.
nodes.domain: One R167 episode, one pre-compensation interval, one fixed consumer and one declared actual-context inventory.

formal_contract_R169.object_domain: actual contexts and local physical interventions
formal_contract_R169.quantifiers: every used node and edge has actual typed provenance; no claim outside the declared connected component
formal_contract_R169.bearer_time_signature: same bearer lineage, fixed consumer, pre-compensation subinterval and realization map
formal_contract_R169.purpose: Replace fitted adjacency by executable physical adjacency

nodes.statement: For every used actual edge {a,b}, a valid structural or simultaneous statistical certificate B(a,b) must upper-bound sup over fixed mediator interventions k in K0 of d_F(Q_{k,a},Q_{k,b}); point estimates, post-result F/K0 changes and shadow-model fit do not qualify.

nodes.scope: Edges of one R169 actual route graph, one frozen K0/F/consumer/timing contract.

formal_contract_R169.quantifiers: every used edge and every k in frozen K0 under one simultaneous-validity event
formal_contract_R169.bearer_time_signature: same actual edge intervention, consumer and time window
formal_contract_R169.purpose: Ground route length in consumer-law units rather than arbitrary labels

nodes.label: Local Channel Budgets Bound Contextual Effect Along Actual Paths
nodes.statement: If every edge has a valid uniform local budget B and D_B is shortest-path budget, then d_F(Q_{k,z},Q_{k,z'})<=D_B(z,z') for every fixed k and |e(z)-e(z')|<=2D_B(z,z') on each certified component; intervention-specific D_k yield the tighter D_k+D_k' form.
nodes.domain: One certified connected component and the same fixed R168 stochastic effect family.
nodes.scope: One certified connected component and the same fixed R168 stochastic effect family.

nodes.counterexamples_and_limits: No bound across disconnected/omitted contexts; the factor-two uniform form can be conservative; actual edge validity remains a premise.

formal_contract_R169.object_domain: R168 consumer-law family on a certified actual route component
formal_contract_R169.quantifiers: every fixed k and every context pair joined by certified paths; supremum over the same K0
formal_contract_R169.bearer_time_signature: same actual consumer, lineage, pre-compensation interval and discriminator class
formal_contract_R169.purpose: Derive effect regularity from local actual routes

nodes.label: Finite-Test Envelope in Actual Path-Budget Units
nodes.statement: With tested upper bounds e(s_i)<=U_i, E_B(z)=min{M,inf_i[U_i+2D_B(z,s_i)]} validly upper-bounds e on the certified component; common eta and direct route fill h_B give sup e<=min{M,eta+2h_B}.
nodes.domain: One common graph component, local certificate family and valid tested-effect upper bounds.
nodes.scope: One common graph component, local certificate family and valid tested-effect upper bounds.
nodes.source_lineage: R169 shortest-path theorem inserted into the R168 envelope argument.
nodes.proof: Apply the R169 effect bound from each tested context and take the infimum/cap; then maximize using the direct graph fill radius.
nodes.counterexamples_and_limits: Not claimed sharp within the kernel-realizable subclass; finite nodes do not cover a continuum without within-cell bounds.

formal_contract_R169.object_domain: tested and untested nodes in one certified actual route component
formal_contract_R169.quantifiers: every node in the declared component under all simultaneous edge and test-bound certificates
formal_contract_R169.bearer_time_signature: same effect definition, route graph and bound-validity event
formal_contract_R169.purpose: Provide a falsifiable alternative to a fitted global L

nodes.label: Envelope Evidence Does Not Identify d and L Separately
nodes.statement: For every c>0, d'=c d and L'=L/c leave every Ld product and the full R168 cone envelope unchanged; envelope data therefore do not separately identify metric scale and Lipschitz constant, while route budgets record their operational product directly in d_F units.
nodes.domain: Any R168 metric-envelope application and positive scalar rescaling.
nodes.scope: Any R168 metric-envelope application and positive scalar rescaling.
nodes.source_lineage: Elementary scale invariance applied to R168's metric envelope.
nodes.proof: (L/c)(c d)=Ld pointwise; all cone terms and their infimum/cap are unchanged.
nodes.counterexamples_and_limits: A unit convention can choose one representative but adds no physical evidence; the discriminator class F remains scientifically substantive.

formal_contract_R169.object_domain: metric and regularity representations of the same envelope
formal_contract_R169.bearer_time_signature: representation-level statement; no new actual bearer inferred
formal_contract_R169.purpose: Prevent a small reported L from masquerading as stronger evidence

nodes.label: Direct Route Radius Dominates the Section Decomposition
nodes.statement: If an actual section r satisfies D_B(z,r(q(z)))<=delta and D_B(r(x),r(x'))<=C d_X(x,x'), then the direct actual-route fill h_B is at most delta+C h_X; a complete actual graph may use h_B directly, but observed labels alone identify neither the graph nor h_B.
nodes.domain: One common R168 partial-view application whose actual contexts and section are nodes of the certified R169 graph.
nodes.scope: One common R168 partial-view application whose actual contexts and section are nodes of the certified R169 graph.
nodes.source_lineage: R168 lift triangle inequality specialized to the R169 route pseudometric.
nodes.proof: Choose the nearest tested observed label and compose fiber and section paths; minimize directly for h_B.
nodes.counterexamples_and_limits: Without hidden-node/edge inventory the R168 two-point obstruction remains; continuum interiors require an additional structural range bound.

formal_contract_R169.object_domain: actual hidden contexts, observed labels, an actual section and a common route pseudometric
formal_contract_R169.quantifiers: every hidden context under all R168 and R169 lift premises
formal_contract_R169.bearer_time_signature: same actual graph, section nodes, tested nodes and episode interval
formal_contract_R169.purpose: Use actual route distance without erasing hidden-fiber obligations

nodes.label: Valid Held-Out Lower Evidence Can Refute an Edge or Path Budget
nodes.statement: If an independently challenged actual edge/path has a valid consumer-law lower bound larger than its declared upper budget, the calibration certificate is refuted; this is distinct from a valid mediator-effect envelope refuting effects above tau.
nodes.domain: One frozen route certificate and an independent actual challenge under the same K0/F/consumer/time contract.
nodes.scope: One frozen route certificate and an independent actual challenge under the same K0/F/consumer/time contract.

formal_contract_R169.quantifiers: existential valid violation refutes the certificate; no converse completeness inference
formal_contract_R169.bearer_time_signature: same actual route variables, consumer and pre-compensation timing
formal_contract_R169.purpose: Make physical calibration rejectable rather than decorative

nodes.label: Invalid, Calibration-Refuted, Route-Certified, or Unresolved
nodes.statement: Invalid identity/edge/timing/measurement gives INVALID_ROUTE_PROTOCOL; a valid held-out lower violation gives CALIBRATION_REFUTED; simultaneous valid local upper and coverage clauses give ROUTE_ENVELOPE_CERTIFIED; all other cases, including omitted or continuum contexts, are UNRESOLVED.
nodes.domain: One named route graph and frozen calibration/challenge plan.
nodes.scope: One named route graph and frozen calibration/challenge plan.
nodes.source_lineage: R168 closure-relative triage refined to separate calibration failure from mediator-effect refutation.

formal_contract_R169.object_domain: one actual route certificate and challenge record
formal_contract_R169.quantifiers: all validity premises precede status; one valid violation refutes; certification is universal only over declared nodes/edges
formal_contract_R169.bearer_time_signature: same episode lineage, consumer geometry, timing and frozen calibration split
formal_contract_R169.purpose: Prevent calibration invalidity from becoming substantive absence

nodes.label: Route Certificate Refines R168 Regularity Only
nodes.statement: If the complete R166/R167 actual witness, R168 stochastic effect/triage and an R169 route certificate all hold on one common episode, the route envelope may discharge part of R168's metric/regularity obligations for that declared component; it does not establish omitted-route completeness, neural realization, C1, B_min, basal experience or an exclusive owner.

rules.statement: At the same supported b,q and for different correct answers, TV(P(C|x,b,q),P(C|xprime,b,q)) >= 1-epsilon_(x,b,q)-epsilon_(xprime,b,q). Without conditioning on B the applicable cut law is joint (C,B), not C alone.
rules.proof_sketch: Fix common supported b,q and use the SAME W_q(.|c,b). Total variation contracts from the conditional cut laws to outputs. The correct-answer event has probability at least 1-epsilon_(x,b,q) for x and at most epsilon_(xprime,b,q) for xprime. For unfixed B, sum over the JOINT cut (C,B); averaging away B can destroy the relevant dependence.
rules.source: R127 theory note §§2,4–5; R130 second review §2

rules.statement: For every nonnegative n-by-n W with n>=2, the positive-edge graph is strongly connected iff for every nontrivial bipartition pi and every vertex i there exists an integer k with 1<=k<=2(n-1) and (W^k-W_pi^k)_[i,i]>0, where W_pi deletes all crossing edges. rules.proof_sketch: For strong connectivity concatenate paths crossing and returning through each cut. Conversely a source SCC admits no closed crossing walk. Parity broadcast on five bits retains one bit; invertible four-bit shift-XOR retains four. Identity and parity modes do not jointly witness full capacity and complete dependencies. Conjugate both dynamics and interventions. Finally Ftilde E=EF since DE=id; induction gives all horizons and majority corrects up to (n-1)/2 pre-update flips per block.

rules.statement: Individual-only categorical labels cannot encode arbitrary successor sets. For a nonnegative membership relation across unique-continuation and fission scenarios, assume full unique continuation gives q(A,B)=1, adding an equally full co-successor preserves that value, and equally full copies are symmetric. Then two full successors have total membership at least 2, incompatible with unit-sum normalization. Equal singleton inclusion marginals need not identify mu; equal singleton inheritance need not identify Gamma. Duplication violates conserved-mass and universal supermodularity; secret sharing violates universal submodularity.
rules.proof_sketch: Use muE(10)=muE(01)=1/2 versus muJ(00)=muJ(11)=1/2. For U=(U1,U2), B=C=U1 and B=U1,C=U2 share singleton Gamma=1/2 but joint scores 1/2 vs1. For U,R independent fair, B=R,C=U XOR R gives singleton0,joint1. Full copies give singleton1+1,joint1. Cardinality and these values prove the remaining clauses.
